name: Conamara Station
note: Original work: a colony on the ice of Europa, over a bore down to the ocean. The geology is real - double ridges, chaos terrain, stained lineae and a surface flatter than anywhere else in the solar system - reconstructed from what is known of it rather than invented. Generated by tools/make-europa.py. Positions are [lat, lon] against an origin at the habitat, on a moon with no agreed prime meridian.
attribution: Conamara Station: original geometry generated by tools/make-europa.py. No assets used.

districts._: [name, hex colour, base height, tallest, box as [lat south, lon west, lat north, lon east]]

landmarks.name: Conamara Station
landmarks.info: Six pressurised drums on legs round a hub, bermed up to the windows in ice - the hard part of living here is not the cold, it is that Europa sits inside Jupiter's radiation belt and the ice is the only shielding anybody has. Nothing touches the ground: a warm thing set on a surface at a hundred and ten kelvin melts its own hole and falls into it.

landmarks.name: The bore
landmarks.info: A hot-water drill running a string down through twenty kilometres of ice to the ocean underneath, which is the only reason anybody is on this moon. Everything that goes down the hole comes back up as vapour and freezes on the way out, so the tower has a permanent plume standing over it.

landmarks.name: The landing field
landmarks.info: Four pads of sintered ice with a blast pit in each. A landing here is completely silent, which is the thing everybody who has seen one says about it first.

landmarks.name: The array
landmarks.info: Sunlight at Jupiter is a twenty-fifth of what it is at Earth, so the panels are enormous and still do not do much; the power comes from the reactor and the panels are a hedge. The biggest structures on the site are the radiators, which nobody ever mentions.

landmarks.name: Conamara Chaos
landmarks.info: Where the ice broke up and re-froze: blocks the size of city blocks, tilted and turned, in a matrix of rubble. It is the best evidence there is that there is an ocean under all this, and the station is named for it.

landmarks.name: The linea
landmarks.info: One of the long cracks, stained brown along both sides by whatever comes up through it - salts from the ocean, most likely. It is the only colour on the whole moon.

space._: Europa is tidally locked, so Jupiter does not rise or set: it hangs in the same place in the sky for ever, twelve degrees across - twenty-four times the width of the Moon from Earth

life._: rovers on the graded lanes, the lights of the site, vents freezing as they blow, and every wheel track ever left here
